questions.text: PAYG Contract Governance: Ensure PAYG contracts are fair and enforceable: (1) Lease-to-own vs perpetual lease clarity; (2) Repossession rights and process (ethical repossession); (3) Ownership transfer documentation (certificate of ownership); (4) Early payoff terms (no penalty?); (5) Default definitions; (6) Dispute resolution clause; (7) Compliance with consumer credit laws.
questions.evidence_required: Contract templates, Repossession policy, Ownership certificates, Legal compliance opinions
questions.africa_specific_notes: Ethical repossession is a major issue. Ownership transfer must be documented (users value ownership). Consumer credit laws often apply.

questions.text: Mini-Grid Connection Agreements: Governance of grid connections: (1) Service level agreement (uptime guarantee); (2) Connection fee policy; (3) Disconnection policy (non-payment); (4) Theft/tampering penalties; (5) Dispute resolution mechanism; (6) Community agreement (MOU with village); (7) Compensation for damages (surges).
questions.evidence_required: Connection agreement templates, SLA documents, Disconnection policy, Community MOUs
questions.africa_specific_notes: Community relationship critical. Theft/tampering common. Disconnection must be fair. SLAs often missing.

questions.text: Warranty Enforcement Governance: Ensure warranties are honored: (1) Warranty claim process (clear steps); (2) Turnaround time commitment; (3) Replacement vs repair policy; (4) Shipping cost responsibility (who pays?); (5) Dispute resolution for denied claims; (6) Tracking system for claims; (7) Regulatory reporting on warranty performance.
questions.evidence_required: Warranty policy, Claim tracking logs, Turnaround time data, Consumer complaint logs
questions.africa_specific_notes: Warranty often empty promise if logistics fail. Shipping costs can exceed product value. Clear process essential.

questions.text: Energy Sector Regulatory Compliance - SSA: Demonstrate compliance with energy regulations: (1) Import licenses/standards (PVOC, SONCAP, PVoC); (2) Energy regulator licenses (ERC, NERC, etc.); (3) Mini-grid permits/concessions; (4) Tariff approvals; (5) Grid code compliance (for interconnectivity); (6) Environmental compliance (EIA); (7) Local content requirements.
questions.evidence_required: Licenses, Permits, Tariff approval letters, EIA reports, Standards certificates
questions.africa_specific_notes: Regulation complex and evolving. Import standards (PVOC) strict to stop counterfeits. Mini-grid licensing often slow. Local content rules increasing.

questions.text: Product Quality Standards Compliance: Compliance with technical standards: (1) Lighting Global / VeraSol quality standards; (2) IEC standards (batteries, panels); (3) National standards (KEBS, SON, UNBS); (4) Warranty standards (minimum duration); (5) Truth-in-advertising compliance; (6) Safety standards; (7) Lab testing reports.
questions.evidence_required: Lighting Global/VeraSol certificates, IEC test reports, National standards certificates, Lab test results
questions.africa_specific_notes: Lighting Global/VeraSol is the gold standard for off-grid solar. National standards often mirror these. Counterfeits are a major governance challenge.

questions.text: Financial & Data Regulation Compliance: Compliance beyond energy: (1) Mobile money/payment regulations; (2) Consumer credit/lending regulations (for PAYG); (3) Data protection laws (DPA, GDPR-like); (4) Tax compliance (VAT, import duties); (5) E-waste regulations; (6) AML/KYC (for high value systems); (7) Corporate governance.
questions.evidence_required: Tax clearance certificates, Data protection registration, Credit license, E-waste management plan
questions.africa_specific_notes: PAYG companies are also fintechs/lenders. Data protection laws emerging. E-waste regulation growing. VAT exemptions often contentious.

questions.text: Consumer Dispute Resolution - Energy: Accessible dispute resolution: (1) Internal complaint handling process; (2) Escalation channels; (3) External recourse (regulator, ombudsman); (4) Village leader mediation (for mini-grids); (5) Response time commitments; (6) No-retaliation policy; (7) Record keeping of disputes.
questions.evidence_required: Complaint procedure, Escalation matrix, Ombudsman contact info, Dispute logs
questions.africa_specific_notes: Formal legal recourse inaccessible. Village leaders/chiefs often mediate mini-grid disputes. Regulator complaints channels exist but slow.

questions.text: Accountability for Service Failures: Compensation and accountability: (1) Compensation for extended downtime; (2) Refund policy for faulty products; (3) Liability for damage (e.g., surge damaging TV); (4) SLA breach penalties; (5) Root cause analysis reporting; (6) Public reporting on reliability; (7) Executive accountability.
questions.evidence_required: Compensation policy, Refund records, Liability insurance, Reliability reports
questions.africa_specific_notes: Users lose income when power fails. Compensation builds trust. Refunds difficult with mobile money/agents but necessary.

questions.text: Technical & Financial Audits: Independent verification: (1) Technical performance audits (mini-grid uptime, voltage); (2) Financial audits (for investors/regulators); (3) Grant/subsidy compliance audits (RBF verification); (4) E-waste audits; (5) Safety audits; (6) Customer satisfaction audits; (7) Data privacy audits.
questions.evidence_required: Audit reports, RBF verification reports, Safety inspection records, Customer survey results
questions.africa_specific_notes: RBF (Results Based Financing) common - requires strict auditing. Technical audits verify quality. Safety audits critical.

questions.text: Community Accountability (Mini-Grids): Accountability to local community: (1) Community energy committees; (2) Regular town hall meetings; (3) Transparent reporting to community; (4) Local hiring commitments; (5) CSR initiatives; (6) Grievance mechanism effectiveness; (7) Social license to operate.
questions.evidence_required: Committee meeting minutes, Town hall records, CSR reports, Local hiring records
questions.africa_specific_notes: Mini-grids need 'social license'. Community committees bridge gap. Local hiring reduces theft/vandalism.

questions.text: Land Rights & Asset Ownership Governance: Ensure ethical land use and asset ownership: (1) Land acquisition process (lease, purchase, donation?); (2) Customary land rights respect (consultation with chiefs/families); (3) Compensation for land use (fair market value?); (4) Asset ownership structure (developer-owned vs community-owned); (5) Transfer of assets (what happens at end of concession?); (6) Dispute resolution for land issues; (7) Documentation of land rights.
questions.evidence_required: Land lease agreements, Community consultation minutes, Title deeds
questions.africa_specific_notes: Land disputes can shut down mini-grids. Customary rights must be respected.

scoring_notes: Layer 3 (Governance) for Energy in SSA: Regulatory compliance (licenses, standards) is baseline. Consumer protection (warranties, fair contracts) is critical for trust in a market with many low-quality counterfeits. Community governance essential for mini-grids.
